newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani vegoil rates seen slipping next week.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani vegoil rates seen slipping next week.

text.p: Pakistani vegetable oil rates are likely to slip next week because of depressed vegoil prices abroad, dealers said on Saturday.
"The downward trend in local vegoil rates will continue in line with the international prices," a dealer at Jalil Brothers Ltd said.
He said rates in the international market have slipped because of increased production and relatively low demand.

Dealers said vegoil stocks in Pakistan fell to an estimated 170,000 tonnes last week from 188,000 tonnes a week ago. RBD palm oil and palm olein stocks fell to an estimated 140,000 tonnes compared to 160,000 last week.

Soybean oil and sunflower oil stocks rose to an estimated 20,000 tonnes from about 16,000 tonnes, while the state-run Ghee Corporation of Pakistan's (GCP) palm oil and palm olien stocks fell to 10,000 tonnes from 12,000 tonnes.

Cielo-Di-Milono is unloading 10,500 tonnes of soyabean oil at Port Qasim. Wawasan Megah with around 25,000 of palmoil is expected to arrive in Pakistan on January 30, while Wawasan Courage is loading 25,000 of palm oil at a Malaysian port. Bunga Chenterawasih and Wawasan Megah will load vegoil for Pakistan at a Malaysian port in February.
